source_document.body:
Walmart has committed approximately $6 billion to expand its work with Symbotic, including additional automation at 25 U.S. regional distribution centers . The agreement covers spending over several years across multiple locations.
What’s Related
The companies said the work will help Walmart store more inventory and improve how products move through its distribution centers. Walmart expects the changes to help it offer a wider selection and replenish inventory more reliably.
The spending covers purchases of Symbotic systems and funding for technology development. According to Symbotic's securities filing, it is an additional commitment separate from purchases Walmart has already agreed to under earlier contracts.
The agreement also provides for work in selected international markets in the Americas. The announcement did not identify the 25 U.S. distribution centers or give a completion date for the upgrades.
RELATED STORIES: Walmart’s Secret to Supply Chain Efficiency | Walmart’s Shipping Boxes Are Too Tall for Its Warehouse Robots
More room for inventory
Walmart said the added automation will support inventory management for its e-commerce business . The work builds on a relationship that has lasted more than a decade.
Rob Montgomery, executive vice president for Walmart U.S. Supply Chain Operations, said: “At Walmart, we're focused on bringing more items to more customers and members, faster than ever.”
Symbotic’s products include BreakPack, which picks individual items, and SymMicro, a small-scale fulfillment system for online orders. Its software uses AI to coordinate case movement through warehouses .
$125 million for new technology
The commitment includes $125 million for research and development of new storage racks and related technology for picking, product movement, and inventory management. That amount is part of the approximately $6 billion total, according to the filing.
Walmart will also pay fees for each system it purchases, including software licenses, maintenance, spare parts, and support. Those fees are in addition to the initial commitment.
Symbotic said the agreement could add up to $6.92 billion to its future backlog, a measure of work contracted for future delivery . The filing also allows the companies to agree to additional system purchases and development programs.
